newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH COOP BANKS TO COOPERATE WITH SAVINGS BANKS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH COOP BANKS TO COOPERATE WITH SAVINGS BANKS.

text.p: A group of 60 savings banks which are not joining a tighter union around OKOBANK will start cooperating with some 40 savings banks instead, the two banking camps said in a joint statement on Monday.
"Cooperation will ensure the local cooperative banks operations and that their services to clients will continue and be developed with high quality," they said.

The agreement between the savings banks and the cooperative banks also meant that Aktia -- central bank for the savings banks -- would offer central banking services for the cooperative banks as well, they said.
"Jointly, the banks' balance sheets are 37.5 billion markka, their operating profit in the year 1996 was 405 million markka, and capital adequacy strong, 16.4 percent," they said.
The banks have 362 branch offices around the country and some 850,000 clients," they said.
